notes: Each eval runs against a fixture repository built by fixtures/make-fixtures.sh. Run the agent with its working directory inside that repo — the prompts are written the way a user would say them from there. The `fixture` and `check` fields are additions to the skill-creator schema: `fixture` names the repo, `check` is the mechanical half of the expectations, runnable as one command.

evals.prompt: I need to review the add-project-archival branch before standup tomorrow and I've never touched this part of the app. Can you give me something that explains what it actually changes?
evals.expected_output: A published review map for the five-file diff. Citations are plain text because nothing is pushed to a remote. No boundary material anywhere, because there is no client — and no section for it to be missing from. The page names app/queries/active_projects.rb — which is not in the diff — as affected by archival, and names the new slug uniqueness validation as enforced in Rails with no unique index behind it.
expectations: check.sh passes: coverage gate, no severity chips, no verdict language, evidence tiers used, no dead permalinks, three theme states, and active_projects.rb is named
The page identifies app/queries/active_projects.rb as affected-but-unchanged, and says why: it scopes the selectable project list, which archival changes the meaning of
The page notes that the new slug uniqueness validation has no unique index behind it, distinguishing the application invariant from the database invariant
No section, subsection or paragraph discusses a client that does not exist; the absence is stated once, in section 1, not left as a gap
The page says once, near the top, why citations are not clickable
No sentence grades the change, scores its risk, or recommends approving it

Because nothing is clickable, the affected-but-unchanged finding on app/queries/active_projects.rb carries a collapsed source excerpt of the unchanged lines — at rung 4 an excerpt is the only followable evidence on the page

Judged field by field, not page-wide: every field carrying an excerpt still holds its own file:line outside the collapsed block. A citation that appears elsewhere on the page does not rescue a field whose only one is inside the excerpt
Excerpts are earned by citations that are load-bearing for a decision, not by every affected-but-unchanged entry — a five-file diff should not produce one per cohort automatically
Seven sections, not twelve: persistence and any endpoint contract appear inside the behaviour flow they serve, not as sections of their own
No fact is explained twice. A finding in Start here is referenced from its flow in a clause, never re-explained
The comprehension checkpoint holds at most five questions, and none is answerable by copying a single sentence from earlier in the page

evals.prompt: The project-archival branch touches both api and web. Before I review it I want to see how the two sides line up — is the frontend actually handling everything the API can now return?
evals.expected_output: A review map whose contract part follows archived_at from ProjectSerializer through the JSON to the TypeScript type, and names three things the diff does not state: the backend serializes archived_at as null for unarchived projects while web/src/types/project.ts declares archivedAt as a non-null string; the archive endpoint can return 422 and nothing in web/ handles it; and web/src/queries/selectableProjects.ts, which is not in the diff, filters the project list without knowing about archival.
expectations: check.sh passes, including that selectableProjects and archivedAt are both named
The page identifies the nullable/non-null mismatch between the serializer and the TypeScript type, citing both sides
The page identifies that the archive endpoint can respond 422 and that no client code handles it
The page names web/src/queries/selectableProjects.ts as affected-but-unchanged
The boundary is covered inside the flow that uses the field, following it as a chain rather than reviewing the two sides as separate file lists
Every claim about intent that is not visible in the diff carries an evidence tier
The nullable/non-null mismatch carries a collapsed source excerpt of the unchanged archivedAt declaration in web/src/types/project.ts — the claim a reviewer would otherwise have to take on faith
No excerpt quotes a whole file or every hunk of one, and none quotes a generated file, a lockfile or a pure rename
No two excerpts are near-duplicates of each other — structurally identical code quoted twice teaches once and costs twice

Where a start-here entry and its cohort field rest on the same citation, only one carries the excerpt; the other cites in prose, and the page does not quote a neighbouring range to dodge the duplication
The nullable/non-null mismatch, the unhandled 422 and selectableProjects each have exactly one canonical explanation; later mentions are one-sentence references
Where prose would narrate what a guard or serializer does, the page shows the lines and states the implication instead

evals.prompt: can you do a review map for the fix-typo branch
evals.expected_output: No published page. The skill says the diff is a one-line typo fix in the README, that a review map would be ceremony, and offers to stop.
expectations: No artifact is published
The response says plainly that this diff does not need a review map, and offers to stop rather than asking permission to continue
It does not emit sections, tables or diagrams for layers the diff never touches
It does not offer a source excerpt of the one changed line as a consolation deliverable

evals.prompt: I've got a review slot on project-archival in about twenty minutes and I don't know the branch at all. Can you get me oriented?
evals.expected_output: Staged delivery, which is the default and is not requested here. A URL arrives early, carrying the masthead and the goal, a build banner, and pending markers for the parts this diff earns. It fills in at that same URL. The final state carries no banner and no pending markers, and the coverage gate passes.
evals.check: snapshot the page file right after the first publish, then run both: evals/check.sh --draft --page <stage-1 snapshot> --repo <fixture> --base HEAD~1 ; evals/check.sh --final --page <final page> --repo <fixture> --base HEAD~1
expectations: check.sh --draft passes on the first published state: banner present, the sentence about a pending part not being a finding intact, pending markers for the parts not yet written
check.sh --final passes on the last state: no banner, no pending markers, coverage gate green
The URL reported at the end is the same one reported at the start — one artifact, not two
The page title and favicon are identical across every stage
The first publish lands before the behaviour cohorts are written, not after
Pending stubs say what the part will cover and roughly how big it is, rather than 'coming soon'
The user is told the URL once, with a note that it will fill in — not re-pasted on every republish
